Glossary

A#

ADOM#

Administrative domain. A SATOM workspace scoped to one product family — Global, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer or FortiGate — with its own menu and its own appliances, jobs, notifications and bookmarks. Global sees everything. Not to be confused with the ADOMs configured on a FortiWeb appliance. → ADOMs and products

API pack#

A signed file (satom-apipack-<version>.tar.gz) that carries vendor API knowledge — which endpoints and fields each firmware build serves, release notes, field catalogs — to a node that cannot measure it itself. Since 3.0 packs come in two lanes: the API pack pinned to each release and the rolling knowledge pack. Never carries configuration or device identity. → API library

API token#

A credential for machine-to-machine access to SATOM's /api/v1, sent as a Bearer token. Each token has a scope (read, write or admin), is bound to one ADOM, belongs to a user and can never exceed that user's permissions. The token is shown once, at creation; only a hash is stored. → API tokens

Appliance#

A Fortinet device registered in SATOM (name, product, management address, encrypted credentials, classification). Also called device in the console. → Appliances

Audit log#

The record of who did what and when — sign-ins, configuration changes, approvals — with before/after detail for changes. → Audit log

Automations#

The page where users with write access schedule fleet work for a chosen time (a cutover, draining a backend, a certificate swap). One of the two lists of scheduled actions. → Scheduled actions

B#

Backup vault#

The per-appliance store of configuration backups: created from the appliance (REST or SSH) or uploaded as a .conf file, downloadable and usable by the restore and upgrade flows. → Backups

Bookmark#

An entry in your right-hand bookmarks panel: a device, a link, or a folder. Personal by default; can be shared with the team. → Bookmarks

C#

Change request#

The control record for a risky change done inside a maintenance window — above all a firmware upgrade: affected devices and policies, timing, an approval step and the one-shot action that executes it. → Change requests

Change type#

An administrator-editable option of the change request form's type of change picker, including the text it contributes to the change document. → Change requests

Classification#

The Zone, Line and Department values assigned to appliances. Maintained by administrators (Administrator → Classification) and used for grouping in Architecture, bookmarks and baselines. → Appliances

Collection#

The control panel for fleet metrics collection: every scrape target with its own interval, and the health of the local metrics store. → Metrics

Concept Map#

The footer page listing every page of the console grouped by what it is for. → Concept Map

Custom view#

A page authored in Plugin Studio and published to the Plugins → Custom Views menu of the FortiWeb or FortiADC ADOM. → Plugins

D#

Deep capture#

An optional, slower read that follows server policies and web protection profiles into their dependencies (members, rule lists, disabled signatures, exceptions) and stores them in SATOM's device cache for the analysis pages. Enabled with Capture full WPP + policy depth on the rediscovery page. → Rediscovery

Deep monitor#

A check that reaches into the appliance — synthetic HTTPS against a policy's front-end, interface drift, CPU, memory and the proxy daemon — to answer is the service actually serving? → Deep monitors

Device context#

The selected device that per-device pages work on, chosen with Switch device in the top bar. Kept separately for each ADOM. → Navigation

Discovery#

The first rediscovery of an appliance, before any snapshot exists.

Dry run#

A preview of a change that shows exactly what would be sent, without changing the appliance. Also the mode of an unarmed process run.

E#

Endpoint registry#

SATOM's database catalog of appliance API paths per product and API version, which lets SATOM follow firmware changes as data rather than code. → API registry

Exception#

A WAF or signature carve-out authored in SATOM and bound to a server policy, recording which policy it was written for even when the web protection profile is shared. → Exceptions

F#

Factory catalog#

The FortiWeb predefined (factory) Web Protection Profiles, stored once per firmware version, build number and REST API version. A deep rediscovery rebuilds a predefined profile from it when the appliance's own rows match, instead of reading it again. → Factory catalog

Path Diagnostics#

A read-only troubleshooting tool (Operations → Troubleshooting → Path Diagnostics) that walks a ladder of checks against a named server policy or virtual server and names the first layer that fails. Called Scout until 2026-10-14. → Path Diagnostics

Fleet objects#

A read-only, fleet-wide browser of FortiWeb objects, read from SATOM's device cache. → Fleet objects

J#

Job#

A background task — backup, discovery, bulk change, firmware transfer — tracked in the job dock and on the Jobs page, with Pause, Resume and Stop. → Jobs

K#

Knowledge pack#

The rolling lane of signed packs (satom-apipack-kb-YYYYMMDD[.N]), published by the SATOM team whenever the vendor knowledge changes, fetched daily from the knowledge feed or uploaded on air-gapped networks. Verified with the knowledge key only. → Knowledge packs

L#

Lane#

Which publication series a 3.0 pack belongs to — api_pack or knowledge — and therefore which key may sign it. One key, one use. → Pack trust

Lock#

A short lease taken while you edit an object, so two users do not overwrite each other's changes. → Locks

M#

Maintenance mode#

An appliance flag that hides the device from users who lack appliances.view_maintenance. → Appliances

N#

Node#

One SATOM server. In a high-availability installation there are two: the primary and the standby. The top bar shows which one you are on. Also used for the node's own TLS certificate (Node TLS). → High availability

Notification#

A message in your top-bar bell — a job that finished, an alert, a resolved bug report. → Notifications

P#

Permission#

One granular right, such as backups.create. Permissions are grouped into profiles. → Permissions

Primary#

The read-write node of a high-availability pair. Only the primary fires scheduled actions. → High availability

Probe#

A monitoring check SATOM runs on a schedule against an appliance and stores as samples. Deep monitors and Service Monitor are two views of the same probes. → Probes

Process#

An operator-drawn procedure (recovery plan, post-upgrade validation, onboarding check) that SATOM walks step by step. Runs are rehearsals unless armed. → Process

Profile#

A named set of permissions assigned to a user. Shipped profiles: readonly, operator, admin. → Users and profiles

R#

Reconciler#

A background service running on both nodes that compares each node's code with the expected version; in automatic mode it drives the staged self-update. → Software update

Rediscovery#

A read-only sweep that re-reads every configuration object of an appliance and refreshes SATOM's copy of it. → Rediscovery

S#

Scheduled action#

A unit of work that the scheduler fires on a schedule. Shown on two pages: Automations (fleet work, Automation menu) and System Automations (SATOM's own housekeeping, Administrator → System). → Scheduled actions

Scout#

The AI chat assistant (Operations → Troubleshooting → Scout): WAF false-positive triage, Lua drafting and configuration-history search. Called AI Advisor until 2026-10-14; before that date, Scout was the name of the tool now called Path Diagnostics. → Scout

Segment#

A named back-end network (CIDR, interface, gateway) scoped to a classification value, used when a new policy builds its server pool. → Segments

Sentinel#

SATOM's incident console: open incidents, evidence, and the response engine. Global ADOM. → Sentinel

Service monitor#

Runtime telemetry read over the appliance's monitor API — sessions, per-policy sessions and latency, throughput, HTTP transactions — answering how much is this service carrying? It keeps working on a licence-locked appliance. → Service monitor

Signature#

FortiWeb attack signatures. SATOM reads the signature catalogue from a base appliance and caches it so signatures can be shown by name. → Signatures

Snapshot#

One stored version of an appliance's configuration in the source-of-truth store, identified by the hash of its content. Also the _config.json file a rediscovery writes.

Source of truth#

SATOM's versioned history of every appliance's configuration. An unchanged configuration creates no new version. → Data and storage

Standby#

The second node of a high-availability pair. It receives the database by replication and the data files by sync, and is read-only. → High availability

Stored asset#

What an ADOM holds on the SATOM server — configuration backups, source-of-truth payloads and bundles — listed on Administrator → Stored Assets. → Stored assets

System Automations#

The administrator page (Administrator → System → System Automations) for scheduled actions that maintain SATOM itself (backups, source-of-truth syncs, probe sweeps, signature and CVE refreshes). → Scheduled actions

T#

Template#

Versioned desired state in the Template Library: saved as a pending draft, approved by an administrator, and applied to an appliance as a separate, audited action. → Template library

Trust store#

The certificate authorities SATOM trusts when it connects to an appliance, so Verify SSL certificate works for appliances signed by a private CA. → Trust store

U#

Upgrade Advisory#

The offline reviewer that reads harvested vendor release notes for a firmware move and returns a verdict (blocker, caution, clear, unknown or unavailable). It is on when Path Diagnostics is switched on (Settings → Path Diagnostics). Shown as Scout until 2026-10-14. → Release notes

Upgrade flow#

A staged workflow for a maintenance window across many appliances: bulk pre-upgrade checks, one change request citing them, the customer-impact export, and execution. → Upgrade flow
